entry.hops: The relay frame (the object executeRemoteFrame returns for a phone) is recorded whole; the phone's JSON text is its JSON.stringify.
entry.notRun: no real room: the host's send throws the refusal
entry.runs: composerSubmitErrorText (renderer), codedErrorParams / ipcErrorEnvelope / ipcErrorFromEnvelope (shared/coded-error.ts), roomMemberSwitchedOffError, executeRemoteFrame (main/remote-methods.ts) with a scripted host that throws, i18n with the catalogs of every supported language

exclusions.renderer: namedTexts, bareTexts, otherMessage, proseWithoutCode, languages, ipcDetails, relayDetails, params: the composer text, the IPC envelope and the whitelist function are the desktop renderer's (apps/desktop/src/renderer/composer-submit-error.ts, shared/coded-error.ts) and stay there; the Rust whitelist is typed (a detail variant per public code) and its length rule is replayed through case 3
exclusions.secretFrame: the first recording of the secret refusal passes the Node capability argument {key}, which is no Rust method's params; case 3 records the same refusal with arguments that are a Rust method's params ("the secret is removed from the params of a public code")
exclusions.storedOutcome: case 4 `status`: Node's relay has no method that reads an outcome back (the frame is `unknown method`), so the core's `op/status` and its rejected-answer notification to a relay connection have no frame to equal; they are replayed against the invariant Node's frames record (`secretInFrames`: no frame carries the call's secret) and against the same read by a local client, from which a relay's differs only by the message and the detail the relay is not told (the call's secrets are not stored with the rejection, so nothing is redacted by them: the text is withheld). The stored rejection is staged in the mock op index (the seam of the app-server tests), not through the core's op gate, which mixdog-core-base replays

normalised.reason: per-run temp path (or generated name) replaced by a placeholder

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay.compare: the desktop relay's refusal frames and the composer's text on the product modules; compare each case whole. In Rust the frame is the server's error answer to a relay connection (error = data.message, errorCode = data.code, errorParams = data.detail): the refusal frames of case 1 and 2 and every answer of case 3 are replayed whole through the real server (mixdog-app-server tests/relay_answer.rs); a failed call asked again (case 4, `first` and `again`) is replayed whole from a second relay connection; the composer's text (namedTexts, bareTexts, otherMessage, proseWithoutCode) and the IPC leg (ipcDetails, relayDetails) are the renderer's and stay on the desktop
replay.entry: Drive these public items on o1: room/send (a refusal of a send to a switched-off member: mixdog-core-rooms/src/rooms/service.rs `failure`, written by mixdog-app-server/src/error.rs `error_data`); op/status and the rejected-answer notification to a relay connection (mixdog-app-server/src/server.rs `op_status_reply`, outgoing.rs `response_rejected`, the refused-decision notification of `on_response`: a stored or forwarded failure is told to a relay without its text and its params, relay_answer.rs `RelayAnswer::stored`); account/saveProviderApiKey, mcp/completeMcpOAuthLogin, connector/addConnectorAccount, mcp/saveMcpServer, approval/provideSecret (the secret-bearing calls whose refusals a phone is told with the call's own secrets removed: mixdog-app-server/src/relay_answer.rs `RelayAnswer`, applied in server.rs `admitted` to a relay connection's requests).

normalised.error / errorCode / errorParams: the members of the JSON-RPC error's `data`: message, code and detail (`name`)
normalised.error.code, error.message: the JSON-RPC error body has no member in Node's frame: the domain error's request-error code and its reason text; they are checked as those constants
normalised.ok: the JSON-RPC answer carries an `error` member and no `result` member exactly when Node's frame has ok:false
normalised.the frame id: none: the replay sends each recorded frame's own id
